title: Quarterly Mosaic Roadmap: Private Instance Lanes, OKRs & Failure Modes
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: This ticket captures the end-to-end quarterly roadmap plan (Q1 2025) for Private/VPC/On‑Prem capabilities grouped into a 'mosaic' of lanes. Each lane corresponds to a customer cohort and an OKR slice: onboarding automation, upgrade safety, RBAC/audit hardening, and dedicated capacity autoscaling. The goal is to produce a prioritized sprint plan, measurable OKRs, acceptance criteria, and an explicit failure-mode register for runbook authors and SRE.

Background: Over the last two quarters we've seen an increase in enterprise interest in private instances with stricter SLAs and complex deployment windows. This plan translates those requests into coordinated work across product, engineering, design, and GTM. It emphasizes observable success criteria that map to revenue and retention signals (activation rate, upgrade success rate, MTTR for tenant incidents).

Scope:
- Onboarding Automation (lane A): self-serve tenant activation, templates for VPC peering, preflight checks.
- Upgrade Safety & Rollouts (lane B): staged upgrades, automatic canary rollback, tenant compatibility verifier.
- Security & Compliance (lane C): RBAC controls, audit log export to KMS/HSM, SSO/SAML flows for private CP.
- Dedicated Capacity & Autoscaling (lane D): reservation primitives, burst policies, cost-hedging signals.
- Observability & QA (cross-lane): route-specific telemetry, acceptance test harness, e2e dashboards.

Trade-offs considered: Prioritizing upgrade safety (B) delays some onboarding UX polish (A) but reduces churn risk for larger customers. Autoscaling work (D) has higher infra cost to deliver in Q1; we propose gated rollouts contingent on a burn-rate quota to protect margins. RBAC/Audit (C) will be built with existing security hooks to minimize scope creep but requires a security review window.

Acceptance criteria (per lane):
- Lane A: 80% reduction in manual steps for first-time tenant activation in our pilot cohort; preflight failure rates < 5% on manifest validation.
- Lane B: 95% automated rollback success during canary failures; upgrade median MTTR < 3 hours for tenants in wave 1.
- Lane C: Audit export to customer KMS implemented and tested against two customers; SSO integration docs published.
- Lane D: Dedicated capacity autoscale by 2x burst for 30m windows with no service degradation and cost delta documented.

Deliverables: sprint backlog, linked PRD (Confluence), design shims, acceptance harness repos, runbook drafts, and a failure-mode register for SRE.

Risks & Mitigations:
- Risk: Upgrade regressions due to dependency matrix complexity. Mitigation: compatibility lab and mandatory preflight compatibility check.
- Risk: Security review delays. Mitigation: early design review with security and weekly checkpoints.
- Risk: Cost overrun from autoscaling experiments. Mitigation: run controlled pilot with telemetry and a billing budget guardrail.

Next steps: align with Eng leads on sprint capacity, finalize PRD, schedule security review for 2025-01-22, and book a GTM readiness slot for 2025-03-10.
